title: Scheduling all single-step refinement requests
statement: Fix a nonempty directed partial-order system V:J→Cᵒᵖ, a presheaf P and distinct s,s′∈colim(V⋙P). Let A be a set of requests, Choices(d) a set of alternatives for each request, Q(d),R(d,k):Cᵒᵖ→Type, q(d,k):R(d,k)→Q(d) natural transformations, and x(d)∈colim(V⋙Q(d)). All indices and request data lie in Type w; P may take values in Type(max w t). Suppose any nonempty directed preorder system T with two distinct P-classes can be refined, for any d and y∈colim(T⋙Q(d)), to a nonempty directed preorder system preserving those classes and lifting y through some q(d,k). Then there is a chain presentation [lem-trf-point-system-chain-union] of a refinement of V, with distinct images in every stage, such that every original x(d) lifts through q(d,k) in some stage.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: Use the full category of good extensions of V: nonempty directed indices and distinct images of the original two classes. Its directed colimits exist. A request is satisfied when the current image of x(d) lifts through one of its q(d,k). Naturality and composition show persistence along morphisms.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: For a missing request, apply the assumed single-step property to its current image and the current two distinct classes. Use the posetal replacement theorem to retain that lift and separation in a partial-order refinement. Compose its embedding with the original embedding, obtaining a new good extension and a morphism from the previous one.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: Apply the scheduling theorem to obtain a good extension satisfying all requests. Present it as a chain with a single stage equal to its entire index. The stage subtype is order-isomorphic to the index; composition and naturality transfer separation and every lifting equation to that stage.
